Conspiracy beliefs

1 Study and sample

The conspiracy beliefs score (conspiracy) was measured in waves 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. Scored N per wave: 500, 500, 500, 500, 500. No respondent is excluded, a provisional rule (decision log D22).

2 Items and coding

Items (guide reference: Imhoff et al. (2022)). Response scale: 1 = strongly disagree, 4 = neither, 7 = strongly agree. Non-answer codes observed: 0.
Item Wording Facet Waves Direction
conspiracy_1 I think that many very important things happen in the world, which the public is never informed about. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
conspiracy_2 I think that politicians usually do not tell us the true motives for their decisions. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
conspiracy_3 I think that government agencies closely monitor all citizens. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
conspiracy_4 I think that events which superficially seem to lack a connection are often the result of secret activities. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
conspiracy_5 I think that there are secret organizations that greatly influence political decisions. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

Score. conspiracy is the mean of its 5 items in the scored direction (higher = more conspiracy beliefs), computed when at least 4 are valid. Scoring rules and names are provisional until the lead signs off (decision log D4, D21).

7 Adjusted model

OLS of conspiracy beliefs on demographics and left-right self-placement, wave 1. Outcome and numeric predictors in SD units, so group terms are differences in outcome SDs. R² = 0.14. N = 453.
Term Beta [95% CI]
Female (vs male) 0.21 [0.03, 0.38]
Age -0.06 [-0.15, 0.03]
Entrance qualification (vs none) -0.10 [-0.31, 0.11]
University degree (vs no entrance qualification) -0.37 [-0.60, -0.15]
Household income band -0.13 [-0.23, -0.04]
East (vs West) 0.30 [0.09, 0.51]
Berlin (vs West) 0.31 [-0.05, 0.67]
Left-right self-placement (right = high) 0.24 [0.15, 0.32]

The model describes associations in this sample. Education groups are provisional (decision log D26), and “another gender” is excluded from the model as too small to estimate.

8 Change over time

Wave means. Analytic N = 500. Self-rated attention subset: N = 480/493/487/487/488. The extract has no instructed-response attention flags, so this subset is a provisional robustness check (Q3).

Mean change from wave 1, random-intercept model (lme4). 500 respondents, 2500 observations.
Contrast Change [95% CI]
wave 2 vs wave 1 0.14 [0.06, 0.22]
wave 3 vs wave 1 -0.07 [-0.15, 0.01]
wave 4 vs wave 1 -0.05 [-0.13, 0.03]
wave 5 vs wave 1 0.02 [-0.06, 0.10]

9 Measurement notes

  • The five items were asked in all five waves with the same wording and scale, so every wave comparison uses the same item set.

10 Reproducing this report

Rebuild with Rscript run.R. Package versions are pinned in renv.lock, and every coding decision is in the decision log.

 

Aggregate results only. Study E is a pseudonymous, embargoed extract; no respondent records are published.
